title: Legacy UFO program secrecy rooted in the Manhattan Project and the 1954 Atomic Energy Act

tellings.quote: specifically legacy programs starting with the same secrecy mechanisms as the Manhattan project and the 1954 atomic energy agreement birthing a lot of the secrecy behind uh UFO legacy program classification and controls.
SEC. 141. POLICY.—It shall be the policy of the Commission to control the dissemination and declassification of Restricted Data in such a manner as to assure the common defense and security.

r. The term 'Restricted Data' means all data concerning (1) design, manufacture, or utilization of atomic weapons; (2) the production of special nuclear material; or (3) the use of special nuclear material in the production of energy, but shall not include data declassified or removed from the Restricted Data category pursuant to section 142.

plain: The idea here is that the secrecy around America's so-called legacy programs, meaning long-running secret programs said to deal with UFOs, grew out of the secrecy built for the atomic bomb. A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb lays it out for Michels. He says these programs started "with the same secrecy mechanisms as the Manhattan project", and that the 1954 atomic energy law gave birth to "a lot of the secrecy behind" how UFO programs are classified and controlled. He draws on David Grusch, a witness who has spoken publicly about such programs, in Grusch's interview with the podcaster Joe Rogan. If he is right, the way UFO secrets are kept would trace back to the nuclear age. The law is the Atomic Energy Act, passed by Congress on August 30, 1954. UAPGerb does not say which part he means. If it is the secrecy rules, the act defines "Restricted Data" as "all data concerning" the design and making of atomic weapons and the production and use of nuclear material. It makes it the policy of the Atomic Energy Commission "to control the dissemination and declassification of Restricted Data in such a manner as to assure the common defense and security." That is a secrecy system built for atomic information. That UFO programs grew out of it is UAPGerb's own step, which the act neither states nor rules out.

discussion.by: Atomic Energy Act of 1954 (Public Law 703, 83rd Congress, 68 Stat. 919)

That the classification and controls of UFO legacy programs grew from that regime is the teller's step, which the act neither states nor excludes.
